candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — identify contraindications, question unsafe IV medication orders, and monitor hemodynamic effects
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — clevidipine contraindication in severe aortic stenosis
candidate.educational_objective: Identify severe aortic stenosis as a contraindication to IV clevidipine and connect that risk with the drug's rapid arterial afterload reduction.

options.A: Clarify the order because severe aortic stenosis is a labeled contraindication to clevidipine due to the risk from afterload reduction.
options.B: Start the infusion because clevidipine increases systemic vascular resistance and therefore supports perfusion across a stenotic aortic valve.
options.C: Start the infusion because clevidipine acts primarily by venoconstriction rather than arterial vasodilation.
options.D: Delay only if the client has renal impairment because clevidipine cannot be rapidly metabolized outside the kidney.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current FDA/DailyMed labeling lists severe aortic stenosis as a contraindication to clevidipine because afterload reduction can reduce myocardial oxygen delivery. Clevidipine is a dihydropyridine L-type calcium channel blocker that lowers blood pressure by decreasing systemic vascular resistance. It is rapidly metabolized by esterases in blood and extravascular tissues, so B, C, and D misstate its pharmacology.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Clevidipine rapidly lowers systemic vascular resistance and is contraindicated in severe aortic stenosis because of the physiologic risk of afterload reduction; its elimination is driven by blood/extravascular esterases rather than renal clearance.
candidate.source_locator: Contraindications, Section 4.3 Severe Aortic Stenosis — contraindicated because afterload reduction can reduce myocardial oxygen delivery. Clinical Pharmacology, Sections 12.1–12.3 — L-type calcium-channel blockade lowers systemic vascular resistance; initial half-life approximately 1 minute; rapid hydrolysis primarily by esterases in blood and extravascular tissues
candidate.source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine DailyMed / U.S. Food and Drug Administration
candidate.stem: A client with severe aortic stenosis has a new order for IV clevidipine to rapidly lower blood pressure. Which action should the nurse take before starting the infusion?
